entries.title: F4 Khipu DAG acyclicity preservation

lean_decls.statement: theorem f4_khipu_dag_acyclic_preserved (es : KhipuEdges) (inv : KhipuBackwardInvariant es) (k : Nat) (newEdges : KhipuEdges) (hk : ∀ e ∈ newEdges, e.1 = k ∧ e.2 < k) : ∀ a, ¬ KhipuReach (es ++ newEdges) a a :=
theorem f4_khipu_reach_decreases (es : KhipuEdges) (inv : KhipuBackwardInvariant es) {a b : Nat} (r : KhipuReach es a b) : b < a := by
theorem f4_khipu_no_cycle (es : KhipuEdges) (inv : KhipuBackwardInvariant es) (a : Nat) : ¬ KhipuReach es a a := by

theorem f4_khipu_append_preserves_invariant (es : KhipuEdges) (inv : KhipuBackwardInvariant es) (k : Nat) (newEdges : KhipuEdges) (hk : ∀ e ∈ newEdges, e.1 = k ∧ e.2 < k) : KhipuBackwardInvariant (es ++ newEdges) := by
theorem f4_khipu_no_self_loop (src dst : Nat) (h : dst < src) : src ≠ dst := by
theorem f4_khipu_acyclic_irrefl (n : Nat) : ¬ (n < n) := Nat.lt_irrefl n
theorem f4_khipu_reach_strictly_smaller (src mid dst : Nat) (e1 : mid < src) (e2 : dst < mid) : dst < src := Nat.lt_trans e2 e1
abbrev KhipuEdges := List (Nat × Nat)
def KhipuBackwardInvariant (es : KhipuEdges) : Prop := ∀ e ∈ es, e.2 < e.1
inductive KhipuReach (es : KhipuEdges) : Nat → Nat → Prop | base {a b : Nat} : KhipuStep es a b → KhipuReach es a b | trans {a b c : Nat} : KhipuStep es a b → KhipuReach es b c → KhipuReach es a c

entries.lean_summary: For a finite Nat×Nat edge list in which every edge (src, dst) has dst < src, every KhipuReach path strictly decreases the node index, so no node reaches itself; appending edges (k, d) with d < k keeps the invariant and therefore acyclicity.

manuscript_anchors.quote: **F4** (the Khipu receipt DAG is acyclic and stays acyclic under append)
appending a backward edge `dst < src` preserves acyclicity of the receipt DAG
now a genuine theorem over a transitive-closure reachability model
#print axioms Lutar.f4_khipu_dag_acyclic_preserved

entries.manuscript_claim: The Khipu receipt DAG is acyclic and stays acyclic under append (Abstract); appending a backward edge dst < src preserves acyclicity (§7.3); A.2 cites Lutar.f4_khipu_dag_acyclic_preserved with axioms {propext, funext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.
entries.gap: §7.3 (L295) matches the Lean model. The Abstract (L21) presents the Nat-indexed edge-list model as the deployed receipt DAG; a deployed store is covered only if it enforces dst < src on every append, which is outside the theorem. A.2 (L450) uses a name that does not resolve at the pin (the declaration is Puriq.Formula.Proved.f4_khipu_dag_acyclic_preserved) and an axiom set that differs from the kernel-emitted [propext] (see P-X2). Minor: hk constrains new edges to source k and targets below k; it does not require k to be fresh, which acyclicity does not need, so the docstring's 'fresh max node' is not a hypothesis.
entries.proposed_wording: F4 [locked]: for a finite Nat×Nat edge list in which every edge points to a strictly smaller node (dst < src), every path strictly decreases the node index, so no node reaches itself; appending edges (k, d) with d < k preserves this. A deployed receipt store inherits acyclicity only if it enforces dst < src on every append. Byzantine agreement is not addressed (Conjecture 2 stays open).

cross_refs.quote: Does not prove acyclicity of a store that admits forward edges, concurrent writers, or Byzantine voters. Does not prove Khipu BFT.

entries.title: F7 Chaski FIFO reception order

lean_decls.statement: theorem f7_chaski_fifo_order (msgs : List Nat) : chaskiDrain (chaskiEnqueueAll [] msgs) = msgs := by rw [f7_chaski_enqueueAll_nil, f7_chaski_drain_eq]
theorem f7_chaski_fifo_positional (msgs : List Nat) (i : Nat) : (chaskiDrain (chaskiEnqueueAll [] msgs))[i]? = msgs[i]? := by rw [f7_chaski_fifo_order]
theorem f7_chaski_drain_eq (q : ChaskiQueue) : chaskiDrain q = q := by
theorem f7_chaski_enqueueAll_nil (xs : List Nat) : chaskiEnqueueAll [] xs = xs := by simp [chaskiEnqueueAll]
theorem f7_chaski_enqueue_preserves_prefix (q : List Nat) (m : Nat) : (chaskiEnqueue q m).take q.length = q := by simp [chaskiEnqueue]
theorem f7_chaski_head_is_oldest (a m : Nat) (q : List Nat) : (chaskiEnqueue (a :: q) m).head? = some a := by simp [chaskiEnqueue]
abbrev ChaskiQueue := List Nat
def chaskiEnqueueAll (q : ChaskiQueue) (xs : List Nat) : ChaskiQueue := q ++ xs
def chaskiDrain : ChaskiQueue → List Nat | [] => [] | m :: ms => m :: chaskiDrain ms

entries.lean_summary: In an in-memory list model, chaskiEnqueueAll q xs := q ++ xs and chaskiDrain is provably the identity on lists (f7_chaski_drain_eq, by structural induction). The main theorem states chaskiDrain (chaskiEnqueueAll [] msgs) = msgs; the positional form states the same with [i]? indexing.

manuscript_anchors.quote: **F7** (the Chaski channel delivers in FIFO order — reception order equals send order, positionally)
replaced two previously-*vacuous* statements (F4 repackaged its hypothesis; F7 was `msgs = msgs`) with genuine, non-vacuous proofs
previously the vacuous `msgs = msgs`, now a genuine positional-ordering theorem
retired the previously vacuous F4 and F7 and replaced them with genuine theorems
genuine FIFO ordering, no longer msgs = msgs

entries.manuscript_claim: The Chaski channel delivers in FIFO order, with reception order equal to send order positionally (Abstract); the 2026-06-10 statement is a genuine, non-vacuous positional-ordering theorem that replaced the vacuous msgs = msgs (§2 rule 3, §7.3, §8.3, A.2).
entries.gap: chaskiDrain is provably the identity and chaskiEnqueueAll [] is the identity, so the main statement reduces to msgs = msgs after two rewrites; its proof is exactly rw [f7_chaski_enqueueAll_nil, f7_chaski_drain_eq]. The model has no interleaving of sends and receives and no concurrency, retries, deduplication or persistence. The manuscript's 'non-vacuous' framing is therefore stronger than the statement supports. claims JSON F7 refinement_gap already says drain is 'definitionally the list itself'; strictly it is provably (by induction), not definitionally, the identity.
entries.proposed_wording: F7 [locked]: in the in-memory list model, draining the queue obtained by appending msgs to the empty queue returns msgs, and the i-th elements agree. Because drain is provably the identity on lists, this records that the model's definitions compose as intended; FIFO under interleaving, retries, deduplication, persistence or recovery is not established.

cross_refs.quote: drain is definitionally the list itself.
